thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: HIGH 5xx spike detected on Dedicated cluster d-helix-03 for tenant=helixdata. 5xx rate jumped from 0.2% -> ~12% starting ~2026-03-15T12:34:00Z. Primary error types: 504 gateway timeout, 500 internal, connection reset. Affected route: POST /v1/generate (inference). Alerting oncall and SRE channel.
oncall-sre-alex: Acknowledged. I'm on it. Quick question — is this limited to helixdata or multi-tenant on the pool?
se-jordan: I'm seeing the same spike in tenant-scoped metrics — CPU and GPU queues on d-helix-03 are saturated for that tenant. Other tenants on the pool show normal tail latency. Looks like noisy tenant or large-batch requests causing inflight queue exhaustion.
eng-runtime-maya: Dumped runtime logs. There's a ton of KV cache thrash and repeated full-model cold-starts for helixdata keys. Also seeing many inflight streaming connections that TTL out with 504. Excerpt:

```
[2026-03-15T12:35:02Z] tenant=helixdata route=/v1/generate status=504 msg="stream timeout after 30s" inflight=256 kv_cache_miss=0.98 gpu_util=99.3%
[2026-03-15T12:35:05Z] tenant=helixdata model=wizard-large event=evict_kv reason=oom
```

eng-runtime-maya: Hypothesis: helixdata workload triggered large sequence lengths + many concurrent requests -> KV cache thrash -> more compute per request -> GPU queue saturation -> timeouts. Could be a combination of request shape and a back-of-the-packet noisy neighbor.
support-evan: Brynn from HelixData pinged support: they report failed requests start ~12:34, ~25% user requests saw errors, customers experiencing timeouts in production UI. They want ETA and workaround.
oncall-sre-alex: Triage plan: 1) Rate-limit / throttle helixdata traffic to stabilize cluster 2) Route new requests for helixdata to fallback pool (if capacity) or to hosted fallback mode 3) Increase replicas on d-helix-03 asap if autoscaler can't keep up 4) Collect heap/kvcache/kvclient metrics and preserve logs for postmortem. I'll try 1 & 2 now.
se-jordan: I can apply a per-tenant rate limit on the gateway. Command below (internal):

```
# throttle tenant to 50rps
rictl tenant update-traffic --tenant helixdata --rate-limit 50
```

se-jordan: Applied. Monitoring.
oncall-sre-alex: Noticed immediate drop in inflight from 256 -> 90. 5xx rate trending down to ~6% now.
eng-runtime-maya: Meanwhile I can reroute to fallback pool using the routing controller. If fallback pool accepts helixdata, it will use a different set of nodes with free GPU headroom. Command:

```
rictl routing reroute --tenant helixdata --from d-helix-03 --to fallback-us-east-2 --mode gradual --weight 100
```

deploy-bot: Reroute job queued. ETA ~45s to finish and warm traffic.
se-jordan: Reroute in progress, starting warm-up of models on fallback nodes. Observability: prefix/KV cache warming is happening; we will see initial higher latency but fewer 504s.
oncall-sre-alex: After throttle+reroute 5xx down to ~1.8% over last 3m. Latency for successful requests increased ~200ms on average. Notify customer that we mitigated immediate errors and are investigating root cause.
support-evan: Messaging sent to Brynn:

"We're aware of the errors and have throttled traffic + rerouted to fallback to reduce failed requests. You may see slightly higher latency; no data loss. We'll follow up with postmortem."

customer-brynn: Thanks — appreciate quick response. A subset of our users still see occasional timeouts but much improved. Please keep us posted if you need sample logs or traces.
eng-runtime-maya: Can we capture a heapdump and kvclient traces from one of the hot nodes before we scale them down? That will help repro.
se-jordan: On it. Taking snapshot now:

```
rictl node snapshot --node d-helix-03-n12 --tags kvclient,heap,openfiles --out /tmp/helix-snap-12-35.tar.gz
```

se-jordan: Snapshot complete and uploaded to incident artifact bucket: s3://incidents/4305001234/helix-snap-12-35.tar.gz
oncall-sre-alex: FYI I'm handing off to night oncall Kevin for monitoring and full root cause follow-up. Notes in brief: noisy tenant caused KV thrash + GPU OOM evictions -> inflight queue saturation -> 504/5xx. Mitigation applied: tenant rate-limit, reroute to fallback. Customer notified. We have snapshots and logs.
sre-kevin: Taking over. I'll keep watch and coordinate with runtime eng (maya) tomorrow for deeper analysis. Any immediate rollback needed?
eng-runtime-maya: No rollback needed. We should run a replay of helixdata request traces on a staging cluster with increased concurrency to reproduce. I'll own repro & postmortem write-up. Assign to me.
support-evan: Customer Brynn confirmed reduction in errors and said they are running a canary release that may have caused higher concurrency. They will share canary config.
noncall-sre-alex: Marking incident severity: SEV-2 due to customer-visible errors and partial SLO breach. Impact window: 2026-03-15T12:34 -> mitigation start 12:38 -> partial mitigation 12:42. Estimated affected requests: ~25% of helixdata requests in that window. Allocated owner: eng-runtime-maya for RCA & postmortem. Handoff owner: sre-kevin for monitoring.
eng-runtime-maya: Postmortem checklist: collect traces, reproduce on staging, identify whether model sequence length or batch shape caused KV eviction frequency, check cache sizing & tenant isolation thresholds, propose mitigations (per-tenant soft limits, fallback routing improvements, early-request-batching heuristics). Will draft within 48h.
customer-brynn: We'll send the canary configuration and some request samples. Thanks for the quick mitigation.
sre-kevin: I'll keep the rate-limit in place for next 2 hours then slowly reduce while watching 5xx. If any regression, I'll reapply stricter limits.
oncall-sre-alex: Closing active paging. If anything flares up, ping @sre-kevin and escalate. Good job team. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident resolved-ish — 5xx rate returned to baseline on d-helix-03. Artifact links: s3://incidents/4305001234/, alerts: https://alerts.redwood/4305001234
se-jordan: Quick follow-ups: 1) Consider per-tenant inflight caps on Dedicated pools 2) Improve warm-start behavior for fallback pool to reduce latency 3) Add a specific alert for kv_cache_miss > 0.7 + gpu_util > 95% for per-tenant context.
eng-runtime-maya: Agreed. I'll include those in the postmortem action items.
support-evan: I'll work with Brynn to sync on a timeline for their canary and coordinate a joint test window.
sre-kevin: Logged in on-call handoff note. Monitoring set. Will close incident channel once postmortem draft requested by Maya is created.
se-jordan: Reaction: :eyes: on the next 2 hours.
end of thread
